issues.title: Comments from Muhammad Usama Sardar
issues.author: antoinepoulain
issues.body:
Original mail at [0].

Could you please expand the discussion in sections 8.4.2.2 and 8.4.3 in security considerations? See some suggestions below. Once this is done, I believe the security considerations are in good shape and we should adopt this.

in #8.4.2.2
Like, you give three examples in 8.4.2.2 which are all genuine, but it would be good to add a little more context to those, and add some references showing where they were actually exploited.

Also, in 8.4.2.2, draft says:
  -> Note that some of these mitigations cannot directly prevent attacks but can be used for detection.
I am curious which ones are for prevention? I believe remote attestation can only do detection and not prevention.

in # 8.4.3
It is not clear to me what you consider as "supply chain" in the context of remote attestation, like is it:
1.	Endorsements and Reference Values? or
2.	the code running in the Attester? or 
3.	supply chain of hardware components? or
4.	some combination of the above 3?

Trojan seems to indicate #3, is it? Draft uses Trojan with capital "T" but does not define it. Is it hardware trojan?
Supply chain attacks can be on the software too (#2), no?


[0]: https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/rats/m0iWplL942mJV5QPKsHWWftGe1c/
